scope: independent visual review of 68 lineage portraits, excludes common pool
method: Compare actual 256px portraits and pre-generation trait contracts; not blinded family classification.

findings.finding: Requested short or upturned broad-tip noses read relatively long/straight at delivery size. Family resemblance is present but exact selected-parent nose transfer is not consistently established.
Requested broad oval face remains comparatively long/angular; father-like facial structure dominates the intended mixed contract.
Broad cleft chin is not clearly legible at 256px; treat as unverified, not exact match.
Brothers show similar nose, mouth and head shape; hairstyle and costume help, but face-only differentiation at 96px may be weak. No literal identical-image clone.
Sisters similarly posed/coiffed and share close facial structure; subtle jaw and cheek width differences, weaker than requested broad-vs-long face contrast.
Corrected old portrait adds facial lines and some greying, but dark copper hair and facial fullness still read near late mature/early old. Older than mature is plausible; exact 65-75 remains REVIEW.

limitations: Independent review by another agent, not a human usability or blinded-family experiment.
This report did not generate either lineage, but had access to trait contracts and identity labels; it is not blind.
Eye hue, subtle brow and exact parent-of-origin visual assignments cannot be certified from reduced portraits.
Age estimates are qualitative, not numeric measurements.
Distinct-person failure persists even where family grouping succeeds.
All 68 selected final lineage PNGs were visually inspected; 11 corrected selections were re-reviewed.

distinctPersonCriterion.definition: At portrait display size, relatives must read as different people rather than the same face with changed hair or costume.

pairs.evidence: At 96px face crop the same narrow long nose, mouth, angular cheek and jaw dominate; hair change does not establish distinct person.
Near-identical facial proportions and mouth/nose despite intended short upturned nose on grandson. Reads as recolored or younger same person.
Minor softness change insufficient at small display size; same eye/nose/mouth configuration and profile dominate.
Face silhouette, nose and smile read as same person; skin and hair differences are slight.
Cheek/jaw width differs slightly, but faces remain very close. Cannot certify distinct identity without larger independent observer study.

distinctPersonCriterion.reviewScale: 256px originals and 96x116 face crops with costume mostly removed
distinctPersonCriterion.note: Visual near-clone failure, not a claim of pixel-identical files.

ageReview.reviewReason: Listed child portraits read between late childhood and early adolescence; specified 6-9 age is not unambiguous. L2 male founder old stage has weaker 65-75 specificity.
supersededFailures: Initial L1 four child stages were adult-like; selected child corrections materially improve proportions.
Initial L1 four mature stages and L2_202_mature had insufficient age separation; selected corrections add visible greying, lines and facial aging.
ageReview.babyObservation: Infants generally read near upper baby range rather than newborns; faces visible. 0-2 category remains plausible.

portraits.traitFidelityNote: Hair color/texture and broad resemblance visible; exact eye hue, brow and selected-parent facial morphology not certified. See specific deviations and near-clone pairs.
